name: Parosh
overview: Parosh is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Pedaiah, as recorded in Nehemiah 3:25. Although his tribal affiliation is not specified, he is mentioned among those who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah 10:14. His presence in these passages connects him to the post-exilic community involved in the restoration of Jerusalem.
namesAndTitles: The name Parosh means 'flea' in Hebrew, as noted in Nehemiah 3:25. This is a proper name and was not given by God. The meaning does not carry explicit theological significance but identifies him distinctly within the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Parosh as the father of Pedaiah, based on the inference from Nehemiah 3:25. Beyond this paternal relationship, no additional family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Parosh's significance lies in his association with the rebuilding efforts of Jerusalem after the exile, as indicated by his mention in the list of those who repaired the city wall (Nehemiah 3:25). Furthermore, his inclusion among the covenant signatories in Nehemiah 10:14 highlights his commitment to the renewed covenant community under Ezra and Nehemiah's leadership. Though a minor figure, Parosh exemplifies the faithful participation of the post-exilic community in restoring God's people and worship.
